2.measure_note: legacy_colAB Schedule A is the UNDERLINE form: rowbands.py returns 17 per-column underline rules (4 segments each) from y=18.21 to y=83.28 at a regular pitch of 4.065, and the four segments ARE the column bands (Date 4.58-16.59, Name of Contributor 18.24-53.20, Mailing Address & Zip Code 54.84-83.62, Amount 85.27-95.75). 17 rules = 17 usable lines (ADDENDUM H1) because THE TEXT SITS ABOVE ITS RULE, so row N spans [rule N-1, rule N] and row 1's band is extrapolated one pitch up from the first rule (14.15-18.21). TWO-CROP PROOF at 900 dpi: the row-1 amount box pct:85.27,14.15,10.48,4.06@p2 rendered the printed 'Amount' header, the filer's '(IN-KIN[D])' marker and the figure '120.00' (recorded 120.00) — so the FIRST WRITTEN ENTRY IS ON BAND 1, the ADDENDUM A1 control passed and no line was skipped; and the ONE-PAST-THE-END control box pct:85.27,30.37,10.48,4.07@p2 (band 5) rendered EMPTY WHITE between two printed rules — no figure, so trap F1.5 (a ledger continuing below the grid) and trap H3 (two entries in one band) are both excluded, and the band list is not off by one. A widened proof strip pct:84.5,14.15,15.4,16.2@p2 rendered all four figures in order: 120.00 / 250.00 / 250.00 / 1,120.00. ROW 4 OVERFLOWS ITS PRINTED COLUMN (ADDENDUM G2): '1,120.00' with a trailing pen stroke runs past the amount column's right rule at 95.75, so row 4 carries an explicit widened geometry string that renders the whole figure; the frame is kept as the honest measurement of the printed grid. Every other row was checked in the widened strip and fits inside the measured band.
